page: Amazon Web Services r8in.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture. It is powered by dedicated Intel processors operating at up to 3.9 GHz, providing 96 physical cores and 192 virtual CPUs via two threads per core. The host features 1,536 GB of system RAM, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory allocation. Operating as a bare-metal server, it provides direct access to the underlying hardware without hypervisor virtualization overhead.

The server does not include integrated local storage, requiring all persistent data to reside on external network-attached volumes such as Amazon EBS. To support high-volume data transport and storage operations, the instance features a 300 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The configuration includes zero dedicated GPUs and does not come with complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

From an architectural standpoint, the system maximizes memory capacity and network throughput at substantial scale. Because local disk volumes are absent, workloads depend entirely on network storage performance, which is mitigated by the 300 Gbps network pipe. Resource density is weighted heavily toward memory and high-frequency core execution rather than local I/O.

The r8in.metal-48xl is structured for memory-demanding enterprise deployments. Key workload fits include large-scale in-memory databases, extensive caching layers, distributed data processing engines, and analytics platforms that require high memory allocations alongside low-latency multi-gigabit network connectivity.
